title: PostgreSQL
subtitle: PostgreSQL is the source of truth for everything I build: a governance work graph, lease-based claiming designed against its concurrency model, and diagnosis from its own tuple statistics.

stats.label: lines in the control plane built on it
tables in the AgentOS work graph

lede: In AgentOS the root problem was state held in a model's context, so I put all of it in PostgreSQL, the one source of truth. Every work order, task, piece of evidence, verdict and cost lives in a relational work graph, and the readable views agents see are generated from it and never edited back. Cost attribution and the effort methodology are computed in PL/pgSQL from the same tables. Schema changes are generated and run against a throwaway database before they touch the real one. See Why long agent runs fail. In FAFO Core and Function Forge many AI and batch workers share one database, so I decided functions read freely and write only through one governed write path.
quote: I build systems around PostgreSQL as the authority that makes autonomous agents' work recoverable and auditable, and the same habits recur across very different systems.
evidence: PostgreSQL schema design: a 546K-line control plane over 88 tables and 79 forward-only migrations, with every agent-readable view generated from the database and never edited back.
Concurrent work claiming: lease-based claiming and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with natural-key writes, so parallel workers never take the same item and a replay adds nothing twice.
Event-driven database design: LISTEN/NOTIFY catalog drift detection with a polling fallback and a hysteresis period before switching back.
Vector data architecture: metadata and lineage in PostgreSQL with vectors kept out of SQL in GPU-addressable shards for high-throughput inference.
author: Corey James
